title: Inference buyers decision storyboard — ops & platform framing
content:
Purpose:
This is a working storyboard for field and SDR teams to frame conversations with platform/SRE/AI-platform buyers who are evaluating managed hyperscaler endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure) versus Redwood. It is intentionally tactical: quick signals to listen for, three buyer narratives, concrete win themes, rebuttals for common objections, and two demo flows that surface our operational advantages. Treat as a live doc — add local anecdotes and customer quotes.

Audience and buyer moments to prioritize:
- Platform engineering (internal inference platform owners) evaluating 'control vs convenience' tradeoffs.
- SRE/ops and reliability leaders focused on latency SLOs, degradation modes, and on-call blast radius.
- Security/compliance folks evaluating private deployments, auditability, and key management.
- Product/ML teams that want consistent API surface across hosted and private runtimes for rollout simplicity.

Top signals that indicate a likely Redwood fit (short cue list for SDRs):
- "We need predictable p99 latency under bursty traffic"
- "Our vendor is throttling during business hours / burst events"
- "We need VPC-only control or on-prem inference for compliance"
- "We want version pinning and canary rollouts for model changes"
- "Costs spiked after model scale — looking to optimize serving costs"

Three buyer narratives (one-liners + expansion):
1) Ops-first reliability story: "Keep the app online under load, even when the cloud provider is overloaded." Expand: emphasize multi-variant fallbacks, regional routing, and deterministic SLOs backed by Dedicated capacity or on-prem. Talk about graceful degradation (smaller model variants, cached prefixes) to preserve essential features.

2) Predictable economics story: "We want unit economics that don't surprise finance as usage scales." Expand: show how batching, KV caching, and quantization guidance can reduce per-token cost by 30–60% vs uncontrolled endpoint usage. Highlight Dedicated commitments and tooling that surfaces token-level spend per route.

3) Compliance & data sovereignty story: "We need to satisfy legal/KYC/regulatory constraints without ripping out product infra." Expand: describe Private offering (VPC + on-prem), KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and the ability to keep control plane in customer network.

Hyperscaler battle themes (short, non-technical positioning for field):
- Hyperscalers win on convenience and breadth of managed stack. They lose on predictable latency under heavy bursty traffic, predictable unit cost at scale, and operational controls for fallbacks. Use customer stories where a managed endpoint had throttling that impacted user-facing features.

- AWS (typical objections): "Bedrock + endpoint is easiest and we already have infra there." Rebuttals: Redwood provides lower p99 in real workloads by applying continuous batching and prefix caching; we offer Dedicated capacity in the same cloud or private VPC to keep data residency and avoid cross-account throttling. Demo hook: simulate a 3x burst and show our autoscale + graceful fallback vs baseline endpoint.

- GCP (Vertex-like): "Vertex gives integrated MLOps + endpoints." Rebuttal: GCP's integrated tooling helps training and model ops, but inference economics and deterministic latency SLOs require a serving-first runtime — we can plug into their ecosystem while delivering consistent latency and lower tail-cost. Demo hook: show a canary rollout between model versions with traffic-splitting and instant rollback on quality drift.

- Azure (OpenAI/Managed): "Azure ties into our identity and enterprise agreements." Rebuttal: identity integration is valuable, but for regulated workloads you still need private control planes and HSM-backed key management; Redwood's Private deployment runs inside customer boundaries and integrates with enterprise identity. Demo hook: audit log trace of a sensitive request showing end-to-end control plane visibility (no vendor logs sent externally).

Concrete win themes and proof points to use in conversations:
- Deterministic SLOs: per-route latency targets and rollback policies backed by Dedicated capacity. Use recent internal benchmark: 95th percentile generation latency stable within +/- 12% across a 10x QPS range (note: internal bench — cite only in field when asked).

- Cost tooling: token-level cost drilldowns and Optimize recommendations that found 38% avg cost savings on a customer pilot by enabling prefix caching + 4-bit quantization on tails.

- Operational control: on-the-wire fallback rules (route to cheaper variant / cached answer) that avoid user-visible failures.

- Integration flexibility: same API surface across hosted/Dedicated/Private reduces engineering lift and simplifies model rollouts and A/B tests.

Objection handling (phrases + scripts):
- Objection: "We can't move off vendor X, it's part of our cloud agreement."
  Script: "Totally. Many customers keep core infra in cloud X — Redwood can sit adjacent (Dedicated in same region) and provide the serving runtime without requiring remote data movement. You keep cloud agreement benefits while gaining bounded latency and clear cost controls."

- Objection: "Latency differences are marginal, why change?"
  Script: "If peak events are rare this may feel fine — but those peaks are when customer experience and revenue are at risk. We can run a 48–72 hour pilot that both measures and demonstrates tail latency improvements under your real traffic mix."

- Objection: "We don't want vendor lock-in."
  Script: "Redwood's API is intentionally simple and we provide migration tooling and off-ramps (model version export, prompt/transform adapters). Our business is being deployable where you need it — you own the model and the data flows."

Demo flows (two short scripts you can hand to SEs):
1) Burst resilience comparison (15–20 mins):
  - Setup: baseline endpoint (managed hyperscaler) vs Redwood Dedicated in same region; pre-load with 1x traffic, then inject 3–5x bursts for 30–60s.
  - Show: p50/p95/p99 across burst window; show fallback kicks in (cached completions, smaller variant) that preserves critical responses; show alerting and rollback on increased error rate.
  - Callout: show token $/route dashboard before/after with small sample billing estimate.

2) Compliance path & rollout control (20 mins):
  - Setup: demo Private control plane (VPC) with HSM/KMS integration and canary model rollout.
  - Show: traffic split, automated quality gating (simple eval on subset), instant rollback, and audit log demonstrating request provenance.
  - Callout: highlight how the same APIs used in hosted mode are used in private mode — minimal code changes for customers.

Quick field-ready snippets (copy/paste):
- "If your current endpoint spikes and throttles, we can run a smoke test in 48 hours to show how Dedicated + caching can protect your user journeys."
- "Most finance teams are surprised by the impact of caching and batching; our Optimize module will give you a prioritized list of changes with estimated $ savings in hours, not weeks."

Open questions for product & SRE to prioritize (please add answers inline):
- Provide a standard short benchmark script that field SEs can run against customer traffic shape (we need a reproducible harness).
- One-pager SLA language for Dedicated pricing tiers (what do we promise for p99 under commitment levels?).
- Quickstart for Private audit log redaction and retention policy examples.

Next steps (owner: Asha):
- Convert this into a 1-pager cheat sheet for SDRs + a 2-slide demo playbook for SEs.
- Align with product on benchmark harness and get an official quote for SRE on SLA language.
- Collect 2 customer anecdotes (anonymized) where endpoints caused visible degradation; add to the demo script library.

Notes / scratch area (raw observations from last 3 field calls):
- Customer A (fintech) lost a late-night feature rollout due to endpoint throttling — they are highly interested in Dedicated capacity for predictable overnight batch inference.
- Customer B (healthcare) needs proof of audit controls before any POC — immediate ask: HSM integration guide and sample audit logs.
- The most persuasive demo moments are when we can reproduce a bad incident and then show the same traffic with our mitigation in place.

If you add anything, prefix with initials and date. This doc will be trimmed into a canonical battlecard once we validate the benchmark scripts.
